items.title: Skillmod
items.text: CBC module for installing approved skills as ordinary files with sup (short for “skill-update”).

items.title: Usage
items.text:
Load this module through CBC, or source it directly in Bash:

source /path/to/skillmod/cbc-module.sh
sup

sup takes no arguments. It installs into ~/.agents/skills/ and reports the GitHub main commit used for the update.

items.title: Update workflow
items.text:
1. Check ~/Documents/github_repositories/skills for a checkout whose origin matches https://github.com/iop098321qwe/skills.git.
  2. If needed, search the home directory for matching checkouts, skipping .git, .cache, node_modules, .venv, and .Trash contents. The search does not follow symlinks. Multiple matches or an incomplete search cause an error.
  3. If none exists, create the parent directory and clone GitHub main into the expected path. An occupied destination is never overwritten.
  4. Fetch main directly from the canonical GitHub HTTPS URL and export that exact commit to a temporary directory. A failed fetch aborts the update; there is no fallback to an older local branch.
  5. Install top-level directories containing SKILL.md, including their supporting files, hidden files, and executable permissions.

The local checkout's branch, uncommitted edits, untracked files, and unpushed commits are not used as installation content. The command does not switch branches or update local branches. Fetching does update Git's object database and FETCH_HEAD.

Matching destination files are overwritten. Destination-only files and skills absent from the repository are preserved, including skills removed from main. User-managed todo.txt files are excluded from exports and copies. No deletion-based mirror operation is performed.

items.title: Moving away from symlinks
items.text:
The first sup run replaces installed skill symlinks with ordinary directories when their names match skill packages on GitHub main. Their original targets are not modified or copied, so local work-in-progress cannot enter the installation through those links.

Unrelated skill symlinks, such as Omarchy-managed skills, remain untouched. Nested destination links that conflict with approved files or directories are replaced without writing through to their targets.

The installation roots (~/.agents and ~/.agents/skills) must be real directories. Source skill symlinks are rejected before installation to avoid copying content from outside the approved export. An ordinary file blocking a skill directory is also reported as an error.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Bash, Git, find, tar, rsync, mktemp, mkdir, and rm.
  • Network access to the GitHub repository when running sup.
  • A writable home directory; paths containing spaces are supported.

The function runs in a subshell to isolate its shell options and cleanup traps from your interactive shell. Temporary export files are cleaned up when it exits. Copy failures return a nonzero status; updates are not transactional across all skills, so rerun after resolving the failure.

items.title: Development
items.text:
Run syntax checks and the isolated integration tests:

bash -n cbc-module.sh tests/sup.sh
npm test

Alternatively, run bash tests/sup.sh without npm. Tests use temporary home directories and a local Git upstream instead of your real skills or GitHub. They exercise cloning, discovery, main isolation, symlink conversion, overwrite behavior, preservation, and error handling.

npm install installs the repository's Husky and commitlint development tooling. Use Conventional Commits. Documentation sources are linked into docs/; .github/workflows/docs.yml builds and deploys the site with Zensical on pushes to main and master.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Guide AI coding agents working in skillmod. All work must follow best practices and industry standards where applicable.

items.title: Scope
items.text: These instructions cover repository code, documentation, tests, and Git work. Source files and tooling configuration define actual behavior.

items.title: Formatting Rules
items.text:
• Keep lines at 80 characters or fewer when practical.
  • Longer URLs, hashes, code blocks, and unbreakable commands are allowed; identify any other necessary exception inline.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text:
• Read README.md and run git status --short --branch before editing.
  • Source cbc-module.sh in Bash to expose sup.
  • Run bash -n cbc-module.sh tests/sup.sh and bash tests/sup.sh.
  • Run git diff --stat before committing.

items.title: Environment
items.text:
• Runtime commands: Bash, Git, find, tar, rsync, mktemp, mkdir, and rm.
  • HOME determines repository discovery and installation paths.
  • TMPDIR, when set, selects the temporary export parent directory.
  • Node.js and npm are needed only for commitlint and Husky tooling.
  • Verification needed: minimum runtime versions are not pinned.

items.title: Repository Overview
items.text:
• cbc-module.sh implements the CBC command sup.
  • tests/ contains isolated shell integration tests.
  • docs/ links root Markdown sources into the documentation tree.
  • site/ contains tracked generated documentation output.
  • .github/ and .husky/ hold deployment and commit automation.

items.title: Tracked Files Overview
items.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml: Zensical build and Pages deployment.
  • .gitignore: local dependency and environment exclusions.
  • .husky/commit-msg: commitlint hook.
  • AGENTS.md: repository agent instructions.
  • LICENSE: GPL license text.
  • README.md: command usage, behavior, and development setup.
  • cbc-module.sh: sourceable Bash sup function.
  • commitlint.config.cjs: Conventional Commits preset.
  • docs/AGENTS.md: symlink to root agent instructions.
  • docs/README.md: symlink to root README.
  • done.txt: completed-task placeholder.
  • inbox.txt.tuxedo-lock: task-tool lock placeholder.
  • package-lock.json: npm dependency lockfile.
  • package.json: test command and development tooling dependencies.
  • site/: generated output; individual files are intentionally omitted.
  • tests/sup.sh: temporary-home and local-upstream integration tests.
  • todo.txt: user-managed task file; agents must not access it.
  • zensical.toml: documentation site configuration.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
• sup runs in a subshell with isolated options, helpers, and traps.
  • Discover a matching origin or clone the canonical skills repository.
  • Fetch GitHub main, pin its commit, and export only skill packages.
  • Exclude user-managed todo.txt files from exports and copies.
  • Merge approved files into ~/.agents/skills/ using rsync checksums.
  • Replace matching destination links; preserve unrelated skills and destination-only files. Never switch the source checkout's branch.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
• source cbc-module.sh: expose sup in the current Bash shell.
  • sup: fetch and install approved skills; mutates the real installation.
  • bash -n cbc-module.sh tests/sup.sh: validate shell syntax.
  • bash tests/sup.sh or npm test: run integration tests.
  • npm install: install commitlint and configure Husky.
  • zensical build --clean: regenerate documentation with Zensical.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
• Tests create temporary homes and repositories and rewrite the GitHub URL to a local upstream through an isolated Git configuration.
  • Verify main-only content, discovery, cloning, updates, permissions, symlink conversion, preservation, failure paths, and temporary cleanup.
  • Never test against the real installation without explicit user intent.

items.title: Linting and Formatting
items.text:
• Use Bash syntax checks and git diff --check before committing.
  • commitlint.config.cjs extends the Conventional Commits preset.
  • No shell formatter or ShellCheck dependency is configured.

items.title: CI and Release
items.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml deploys Pages on main and master pushes.
  • CI installs Zensical and runs zensical build --clean.
  • Use Conventional Commits with standalone, changelog-ready headers and supplemental bodies. Select the type from the actual change impact.
  • Prefer amending small related corrections into the relevant current branch commit when explicitly authorized and history is unpublished; avoid unnecessary fixup or cleanup commits.
  • Never edit CHANGELOG.md manually; generated changelogs belong to release tooling. No release filters are configured in this repository.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Keep the module sourceable; loading it must not perform an update.
  • Check failures explicitly so if sup callers also stop on errors.
  • Keep README and AGENTS changes in separate docs-only commits.
  • Agents must never read, create, edit, delete, move, stage, commit, or otherwise touch todo.txt; only the user may modify it manually.
  • Keep instructions concise and free of update notes or work logs.

items.title: Security and Compliance
items.text:
• Never commit secrets, credentials, tokens, or private keys.
  • Fetch installation content from the canonical GitHub URL, not local branches or working-tree files.
  • Reject source symlinks and linked installation roots before copying.
  • Do not follow destination symlinks when overwriting approved paths.

items.title: Dependencies and Services
items.text:
• sup uses https://github.com/iop098321qwe/skills.git over HTTPS.
  • rsync merges files without --delete and preserves executable modes.
  • Development uses Husky and commitlint from package.json.
  • Docs deployment uses Zensical and GitHub Pages.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• A failed fetch must abort without falling back to stale local content.
  • For ambiguous discovery, place the intended checkout at the expected path documented in README.md.
  • Resolve occupied clone paths, linked roots, source links, and file conflicts before retrying. Copy failures may leave partial updates.
  • Edit root Markdown sources, not their docs/ symlinks or generated site.

items.title: Refining Existing AGENTS.md
items.text:
• Verify every statement against the repository before keeping it.
  • Remove stale, duplicated, or vague guidance and any update logs.
  • Replace placeholders with exact verified commands and paths.
  • Keep bullets short and preserve this section order.
  • Mark unverified claims with the exact verification still needed.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text:
• After code, configuration, or docs changes, compare this file with the current source, tests, dependencies, and tracked file inventory.
  • Recheck commands, paths, runtime requirements, and automation.
  • Update mismatches in a separate docs Conventional Commit.
  • Preserve the user-only task-file rule; never append maintenance logs.
